purpose: An offline consumer can show an original fictional maintenance queue without double-counting repeated receipts.

fields.classification: Always SYNTHETIC. Never display as real player telemetry.
fields.release_authority: Always false. No approvals may be inferred.
fields.input_sha256: Lowercase SHA-256 of the selected UTF-8 file's exact bytes.
fields.input_records: Count of all validated nonblank records, including repeats.
fields.open_queue: Sorted item IDs whose final state is open; a queue, not a deployment gate.

summary.event_count: Unique event IDs after complete conflict validation.
summary.open_items: Number of item rows with state open.
summary.closed_items: Number of item rows with state closed.
summary.items: Rows sorted by item_id, containing item_id, state, unique event_count, and last_minute.

input_rules: Each strict JSONL record has classification, event_id, item_id, action, and at_minute only.
Conflicting payloads for an existing event ID are errors, not a last-write-wins update.
Different IDs remain different events, even when all other fields match.
Chronological order uses (at_minute, event_id), not arrival time or the host clock.
The raw input is not mutated. The CLI writes only stdout or a diagnostic to stderr.

cli_exit_codes.2: Invalid invocation, input, or selected-file error.

integration_status: Artifact provided and tested; no other workstream was modified and no Pocket Arcade integration is claimed.
limitations: Python 3.9+ standard library; no network dependencies.
At most 1 MiB, 16 KiB per line, 5000 raw records, 40 characters per ID, and integer minutes from 0 through 1000000.
Only explicitly synthetic fixtures are accepted; this is not a production event broker or security audit.
